hero.title: Literary Sources of Buddhism
hero.description: An analytical study of the canonical and non-canonical texts that shaped the doctrinal foundation of Buddhist philosophy in Ancient India.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Canons

  • Pali Canon (Tipitaka)
  • Sanskrit Sutras (Mahayana)

Key Texts

  • Jataka Tales
  • Milinda Panho
  • Dipavamsa/Mahavamsa

Mindmap of Buddhist Literature

  • Tipitaka (The Three Baskets)
    • Vinaya Pitaka: Rules of Monastic order.
    • Sutta Pitaka: Buddha's discourses (Five Nikayas).
    • Abhidhamma Pitaka: Metaphysical/Philosophical analysis.
  • Non-Canonical/Commentary
    • Jataka: Stories of previous births.
    • Milinda Panho: Dialogue between Nagasena and Menander.
    • Ceylonese Chronicles: Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa (History).

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Evolution of Buddhist literature from oral traditions to codified Pali and Sanskrit canons.

cards.details: First Buddhist Council at Rajgriha; oral compilation of Vinaya and Sutta Pitakas.
Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra; Abhidhamma Pitaka added; Missions sent to Sri Lanka.
Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir; Rise of Mahayana and Sanskrit Buddhist literature (e.g., Saundarananda).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Thinking Tripitakas were written down during the Buddha's lifetime (They were oral traditions for centuries).
Confusing Mahayana texts (Sanskrit) with Theravada/Hinayana texts (Pali).
